title: Check: Reactions of Acids with Metal Oxides (2)

questions.stem: Why is the reaction between a metal oxide and an acid classified as a neutralisation reaction?

options.text: Because metal oxides are bases that neutralise acids to form salt and water

questions.explanation: Metal oxides are bases because they contain oxide ions (O²⁻) that accept H⁺ ions from the acid. The reaction O²⁻ + 2H⁺ → H₂O forms water, making it a neutralisation reaction. The products are always a salt and water.

questions.stem: When making a salt from a metal oxide and an acid, why is excess metal oxide added?

options.text: To make the reaction go faster
To ensure all the acid has reacted, since excess solid can be filtered off
To change the colour of the salt

questions.explanation: Excess metal oxide is added to ensure all the acid has reacted, so the salt solution is not contaminated with unreacted acid. The excess insoluble solid is easily removed by filtration, leaving a pure salt solution.
